 ORDER 1.

Appellants have preferred this appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred as "MV Act") for the enhancement of the compensation amount awarded in Claim Case No.3382/2018 passed by the 25th Addl. Member, MACT, Indore on 9.9.2022, whereby an amount of Rs.15,87,688/- was awarded to the appellants/claimants towards the compensation.

2. The relevant and necessary facts of the case are that on 6.6.2018 at about 11.30 p.m. when the deceased Devilal was going towards Chandan Nagar on the motorcycle, when he reached near the Chandan Nagar Square, at the same time driver of the offending vehicle bearing registration No.MP09-LP- 0796/respondent No.1 driven the vehicle rashly and negligently and dashed the said motorcycle very badly, due to which Devilal sustained fatal injuries on the vital parts.
He was admitted in the hospital.
On the next day he has been died.
Accordingly offence has been registered.

3. Learned counsel for the appellants/claimants preferred a claim petition before the below Tribunal under Section 166 of the MV Act by submitting that the appellant No.1 is the widow of the deceased and appellant No.4 is the mother of the deceased and appellants No.2 & 3 are the sons of the deceased.
Deceased was 33 years old person.
He was doing building contractorship and earning more than Rs.25,000/- per month.
Appellants were dependent upon his income.
They have been deprived from the earning of the deceased.
Vehicle was insured with respondent No.2/insurance company.
4. Respondent No.1 remained absent before the below Tribunal, therefore, the matter was tried ex parte against him.

Respondent No.2 denied all the averments of the claim petition by submitting that at the time of accident driver of the motorcycle was not having any valid and effective licence and motorcycle was being driven in violation of the insurance policy.
Respondent No.1 also violated the terms and conditions of the insurance policy, therefore, appellants are not entitled for any compensation.

5. The claims Tribunal after framing the issues and recording evidence and after appreciating the evidence available on record, partly allowed the claim petition by passing an award of Rs.15,87,688/- towards the compensation along with interest @6% per annum.
Being aggrieved by the findings given by the below Tribunal, this appeal has been preferred by the appellants.
6. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the below Tribunal has committed error in assessing the annual income of the deceased.
Deceased was working as a contractor.
The below Tribunal has not considered the factum of number of 4 dependents, children's education, food and living.

Below tribunal has not applied the correct multiplier and not assessed the future income of Smt. Sangeeta vs Krishnamurari on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115152954/
2 the deceased.
Hence, he prays for enhancement of the compensation amount awarded by the below Tribunal.
7. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent No.2 opposes the prayer by submitting that the impugned award is just, proper and adequate and not deserve for any interference.
8. I have heard learned counsel for both the parties at length and perused the record.

9. From perusal of the evidence available on record, it is proved that the said accident was caused by the offending vehicle which was being driven by the respondent No.1 and the offending vehicle was duly insured with respondent No.2.
There is no material available on record to establish that there was any breach of the insurance policy by the owner or driver of the offending vehicle.
10. The moot question to be addressed in the appeal preferred by the appellants is, as to whether the Tribunal was justified in awarding Rs.15,87,688/- to the appellants?
11. The below Tribunal has considered the deceased's monthly income as Rs.7057/-.

Although it is contended that the deceased was building contractor but no registration certificate of the contractor has been proved by the claimants and no relevant document regarding the income tax of the deceased was filed.

The accident has occurred in the year 2018, therefore, as per the guideline issued by the Labour Commissioner, Indore and also looking to the fact that deceased was unskilled labour,
his income ought to have been determined as Rs.8,182/- per month.
Deceased was 40 years old at the time of accident, therefore, the below Tribunal has rightly applied the multiplier of 16.

In the light of the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Vs. Pranay Sethi reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157, the below Tribunal has rightly awarded 40% amount towards future prospects.

sentences.text:
Therefore, the loss of dependency comes to Rs.98,184/- (-) Rs.24,546/- (1/4th deduction) = Rs.73,638/- x 16 = Rs.11,78,208/- Rs.4,71,283/- (40% future prospects) =
Rs.16,49,491/-.
The amount awarded by the Tribunal under the other heads is just and proper.
12. In view of the above, the appellants are entitled to Rs.16,49,491/- under the head of loss of dependency, whereas the below Tribunal has awarded only Rs.14,22,688/- under this head.
13. Accordingly, the appeal is partly allowed.
The compensation as awarded by the tribunal deserves to be and is accordingly enhanced by a sum of Rs. 2,26,803/-.
The enhanced amount will bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the tribunal and will be governed by the same conditions as contained in the award of the tribunal.
No order as to costs.
C.C. as per rules.
